teaser.text: Netflix sells a monthly pass to entertainment delivered over the internet. The business works when the catalogue keeps households paying, while Netflix turns those payments into programmes, delivery and profit.

stock.opening: Netflix's weighted forecast is $65.87 in October 2027 and $90.74 in October 2029. It hinges on advertising monetization, retention and disciplined content spending.
stock.closing: The full Netflix memo also examines Netflix’s business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast is $65.87 in October 2027 and $90.74 in October 2029. It assigns 25% probability to the bear case, 55% to the base case and 20% to the bull case. The forecast expects a weak first year followed by gains.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Netflix?

paragraphs.text: The bear case requires advertising to miss its ramp while live and other content costs fail to produce lasting retention. Earnings fall, margins compress and the multiple declines. The price is $43.19 in October 2027. It reaches $34.96 by October 2029.

The bull case reaches $86.78 first and $142.87 last. Its 20% probability reflects the need for faster ad monetization, durable event-driven retention and stronger margins at the same time. Netflix reports that live events produced six of its ten biggest new-member sign-up days, but the material does not establish lasting retention or title-level returns.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Netflix really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is operating cash flow less purchases of property and equipment. It reached 9,461,053 in 2025, or 20.9% of revenue. Subtracting stock-based compensation produces an analytical “real free cash flow” of 9,092,604, though that adjustment is not Netflix’s own cash-flow definition.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Netflix?

paragraphs.text: The price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, shows how much investors pay for each dollar of annual profit. The trailing version uses the last twelve months; the forward version uses the next twelve months’ expected profit. The forward multiple is lower because expectations assume earnings will rise. But the share price can still fall if earnings miss or investors decide the multiple is too generous.

earnings.title: Netflix earnings: guidance and next results
earnings.meta_description: Netflix reports on October 20, 2026; guidance is $51,000–$51,400 million revenue and 13.0%–14.0% growth.
earnings.opening: Netflix reports its next results on October 20, 2026. The key thing to watch is advertising monetization.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers what Netflix does, who its rivals are, how management operates, and what risks could shape its future.

paragraphs.text: Netflix expects 2026 revenue of $51,000–$51,400 million, or growth of 13.0%–14.0%. Subscriptions, price increases and advertising must produce that result together. Its foreign-exchange-neutral growth forecast is 12.0%, which shows how much the business itself is expected to grow without changes in currency values.

Management expects content amortization to rise 10.0% in 2026 and maintains free-cash-flow guidance of approximately $12,500 million. Free cash flow is operating cash received minus operating payments and equipment purchases. The annual forecast benefited from a Warner Bros. transaction termination fee in Q1, while higher cash taxes weighed on Q2, so one quarter multiplied by four would mislead.

blocks.heading: Did Netflix keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Bonuses also emphasize operating margin, the share of sales left after operating expenses, more heavily than revenue. Management forecast 2025 revenue of US$43.5–44.5 billion in April and finished with US$45.2 billion. Advertising revenue grew to more than 2.5 times the previous year’s level, supporting the case that management delivered against its early plan.

blocks.heading: How have Netflix's revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: Revenue reached 12,559,938, up 13.4% from the prior-year quarter. Every region grew, and currency-neutral growth was approximately 12%, which means exchange rates helped the reported result. Membership growth, pricing and advertising all contributed, but the missing subscriber and ARM bridge prevents precise attribution.

blocks.heading: What should Netflix watch in its next release?

paragraphs.text: Advertising deserves separate attention. A strong total-revenue quarter could still hide a slow advertising ramp, so investors should look for evidence that Netflix is selling more of its available opportunities at useful prices. They should also ask whether any profit surprise reflects lasting improvement or expenses moving between quarters.
